headline: New Hampshire bald eagle fledglings reach 100 for first time in decades
dek: NH Audubon says 100 bald eagle chicks fledged from 64 nests this year, marking a new milestone in the state's recovery of the once-endangered species.
body: New Hampshire recorded 100 bald eagle fledglings from 64 nests during the 2026 breeding season, the first time the statewide total has reached triple digits since NH Audubon began tracking the species in 1989.

The milestone represents a 17.85% increase from the 85 fledglings confirmed in 2025, according to NH Audubon's season results. Monitors also documented 107 territorial pairs, 85 pairs that incubated eggs and four nests with three chicks each; last year, one nest had three chicks.

The recovery follows decades of monitoring by NH Audubon, New Hampshire Fish and Game and volunteer nest observers. NHPR reported that the state's program began after bald eagles were pushed near extinction by DDT, which weakened eggshells; the species was removed from New Hampshire's endangered-species list in 2017.

Researchers banded 20 chicks at 10 nests in partnership with Maine's Biodiversity Research Institute and collected samples for testing for avian influenza, mercury and PFAS. NH Audubon said the work will help track the population as rodenticides and disturbance around nests remain ongoing concerns.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: New Hampshire bald eagle fledglings reach 100
seoDescription: NH Audubon reports a record 100 bald eagle fledglings from 64 New Hampshire nests during the 2026 breeding season.
